messages:
Ashley Park: Quick sync — we need a tighter battlecard for launch week that differentiates Redwood from cloud AI platforms + API-first vendors. Focus: unit economics, predictable SLOs, private deployment, and observability hooks. Short bullets and rebuttals only.
Matt Cole: Agree. Can we get 3 lead soundbites for SDRs and 3 rebuttals for sales? Keep <30 char headlines for slides.
Jin Wei: I sketched a few one-liners in the doc: 
- "Costs you can forecast, not guess" — highlights Dedicated/Reserved capacity
- "Same API, stronger guarantees" — unified runtime + SLAs
- "Private by design, portable by default" — VPC & on-prem story
Sara Lopez: Love those. For cloud APIs objection ("we already use X cloud"), a quick riposte: 
- Sales: "If latency and cost vary with usage, we make predictability a lever, not a risk."
- For infra vendors (self-hosted runtimes): "You can build it, or you can run it reliably at scale — we do the latter with SLOs and rollout tooling."
Ida Gupta: Add a short technical proof point: "Smart routing + KV/prefix cache = 2x token cost savings on conversation patterns we benchmarked." That helps engineering buyers.
Matt Cole: Can we make the benchmarking claim less numeric/unless we have the slide: maybe "benchmarked token savings on chat workloads" and call out the eval lab slide.
Jin Wei: Good call. Also add a short snippet for the webinar opener: "Most teams move from prototype to product and realize models are only half the problem — serving is everything else."
Ashley Park: We need 3 rapid objections and rebuttals deck-ready:
1) "Cloud vendor gives me models + infra" -> "They sell models; we sell predictable inference economics with rollouts, fallback policies, and private deployments tied to SLAs."
2) "We can run open models ourselves" -> "You can, but running at 99% P99 latency with cost controls and KV cache is non-trivial — we ship that operability."
3) "Price looks lower on raw GPU hours" -> "Unit economics are about tokens served under SLO — we optimize batching, cache, and quantization to lower per-token costs while preserving quality."
Sara Lopez: For SDR scripts: quick hooks — "We reduce inference cost variability, not just average cost." and "We give you the fallback plan when capacity goes soft."
Ida Gupta: Also call out observability: "token-level cost + latency traces and per-prompt regression alerts" — that's a legit differentiator for platform teams.
Matt Cole: Webinar CTA: field-validated checklist + battlecard download for field — make the form gated so AE gets lead score (tier by infra need).
Ashley Park: Assigned: Jin -> polish one-liners, Sara -> SDR scripts & webinar copy, Matt -> sales rebuttal bullets + gating plan, Ida -> technical playbook proof points. Deadline EOD Wednesday.
deploy-bot: Reminder: marketing-assets pipeline job queued for 3729990200 — will lint copy and upload slides to /launch/benchmarks if approved.
Jin Wei: Will push updated snippets by EOD. Quick ask: can someone pull the latest benchmark numbers for chat-batch patterns? Need the exact phrasing.
Ida Gupta: I'll pull the numbers and add conservative language ("benchmarked savings on typical chat workloads").
Sara Lopez: I'll draft two SDR email versions (short and long) and post in #marketing-drafts before lunch tomorrow.
Matt Cole: I'll draft sales rebut bullet cards and short roleplay lines for the webinar panel.
Ashley Park: Perfect — we'll review Thursday morning and lock the battlecard. Tiny request: avoid the word "best" anywhere. Use concrete levers (routing, caching, SLAs).
Jin Wei: Noted. Sending updates tonight. :thumbsup:
Ashley Park: Thanks team — feel free to @me when drafts are up.
